neighbours.label: the 'if' that opens a concessive 'X, if not Y,' aside inside a clause (widely, if not universally), as opposed to conditional 'if' or a 'though not' aside
fire: The treaty was broadly, if not unanimously, welcomed by the delegates.
Her claim is now usually, if not always, taken at face value by historians.
Most of the villagers were sceptical, if not openly hostile, toward the plan.
The method is rarely, if ever, used in modern hospitals.
The bridge was badly, if not fatally, damaged by the flood.
His second novel was largely, if not entirely, ignored by critics.
The results were promising, if not conclusive, for the research team.
The old mill is mostly, if not completely, abandoned these days.
quiet: The treaty was broadly welcomed by the delegates at the summit.
Her claim is now usually taken at face value, though not always, by historians.
If the villagers were sceptical, the council would delay the plan.
The method is rarely used in modern hospitals because it is slow.
If the bridge was damaged by the flood, the road would be closed.
His second novel was largely ignored, but not entirely, by critics.
The results were promising for the research team, though not conclusive.
Ask the miller if the old mill is still open these days.

predictions: fire 0.25-0.45 on ' if' of 'A, if not B,'; conditional 'if' and 'though not' asides below 0.15
